# Renames Checkout initialization method

## What’s new

Renames the `stripe.initCheckout()` method for [Stripe.js](https://docs.stripe.com/js.md) to [stripe.initCheckoutElementsSdk()](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/init). It accepts the same options and returns the same Checkout object as `initCheckout()`.

Additionally, introduces `stripe.initCheckoutFormSdk()` as a new entry point for [Checkout form](https://docs.stripe.com/checkout/form/quickstart.md) integrations. Use `initCheckoutFormSdk()` instead of `initCheckoutElementsSdk()` when your integration uses `ui_mode: "form"`.

## Why is this a breaking change?

`stripe.initCheckout()` has been renamed, so calling it throws an `IntegrationError`. If your integration uses [Elements with the Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md) and calls `initCheckout()`, you need to update your code to instead call `initCheckoutElementsSdk()`.

The update depends on whether you use HTML+JS or React:

#### HTML + JS

Replace `stripe.initCheckout()` with `stripe.initCheckoutElementsSdk()`:

```javascript

const checkout = stripe.initCheckoutElementsSdk({clientSecret});
```

#### React

Replace `CheckoutProvider` with `CheckoutElementsProvider`:

```jsx

import {CheckoutElementsProvider} from '@stripe/react-stripe-js/checkout';

<CheckoutElementsProvider stripe={stripePromise} options={{clientSecret}}>
<CheckoutForm />
</CheckoutElementsProvider>
```

If you use the Payment Form Element, use a [Checkout form](https://docs.stripe.com/checkout/form/quickstart.md). The update depends on whether you use HTML+JS or React:

#### HTML + JS

Replace `stripe.initCheckout()` with `stripe.initCheckoutFormSdk()` and use `createForm()` from the returned Checkout form SDK:

```javascript

const checkoutFormSdk = stripe.initCheckoutFormSdk({clientSecret});
const checkoutForm = checkoutFormSdk.createForm();
```

#### React

Replace `CheckoutProvider` with `CheckoutFormProvider` and use the new `CheckoutForm` export from `@stripe/react-stripe-js` instead of the `PaymentFormElement`:

```jsx

import {CheckoutFormProvider, CheckoutForm} from '@stripe/react-stripe-js/checkout';

<CheckoutFormProvider stripe={stripePromise} options={{clientSecret}}>
<CheckoutForm />
</CheckoutFormProvider>
```

## Impact

The rename from `initCheckout` to `initCheckoutElementsSdk` clarifies the method’s purpose as the entry point for [Elements with Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md) integrations, where you compose individual Elements (Payment Element, Address Element, and so on) on your checkout page.

The new `initCheckoutFormSdk()` method provides a dedicated entry point for [Checkout form](https://docs.stripe.com/checkout/form/quickstart.md) integrations, corresponding to `ui_mode: "form"`.

## Related changes

- [Changes the Address Element state field to default to Latin-formatted characters](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia/2026-03-25/address-element-getvalue-and-change-event-formatting.md)

- [Removes support for boolean values in options.layout.radios](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia/2026-03-25/disallow-booleans-for-radios.md)
- [Removes deprecated Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and Sources methods from Stripe.js](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia/2026-03-25/remove-legacy-stripejs-methods.md)
- [Renames Embedded Checkout initialization method](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia/2026-03-25/rename-init-embedded-checkout-to-create-embedded-checkout-page.md)

# Updates Checkout Session UI mode enum values

## What’s new

Updates the [ui_mode](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#create_checkout_session-ui_mode) parameter for [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#checkout_session_object-ui_mode) to use the following clearer, more descriptive enum values:

# Updates the events_from parameter on event destinations to accept string values

## What’s new

Updates the [events_from](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/event-destinations/create.md?api-version=2026-03-25.dahlia#v2_create_event_destinations-events_from) parameter on the `EventDestination` object to be a nullable array of strings instead of a nullable array of enums. It accepts the following strings:

- `@self`: events from the account that owns the destination (replaces the `self` enum value)
- `@accounts`: events from connected accounts of your platform account (replaces the `other_accounts` enum value)
- `@organization_members`: events from accounts in your organization
- `@organization_members/@accounts`: events from connected accounts of platform accounts in your organization

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `events_from` parameter changes from an enum type to a string type and uses different values. SDK type definitions that previously used a typed enum union (`self` | `other_accounts`) must now use `string`. If your integration expects the previous values, you need to update your code to expect the new values.

## Impact

You can now set the `events_from` parameter to one of 4 string values when creating event destinations instead of using the previous 2 enum values. Update any code that checks for specific `events_from` values in API responses to expect the new values.

The API continues to accept the previous values as input, so you don’t have to update your code for creating destinations. However, Stripe automatically converts the enum values to the corresponding string values. For example, if you set the value to `self`, it becomes `@self`. You need to update any code that expects it to be `self`.

## Changes

#### REST API

| Fields | Change | From → to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `V2.Core.EventDestination#create.events_from`, `V2.Core.EventDestination.events_from` | Changed | `enum('other_accounts'|'self') → string` |

#### Node.js

| Fields | Change | From → to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `V2.Core.EventDestination.events_from`, `V2.Core.EventDestinationCreateParams.events_from` | Changed | `enum('other_accounts'|'self') → string` |

# Adds address validation errors for CMRAs and registered agents to Accounts v1 and Accounts v2

## What’s new

Adds two values to the [requirements.errors[].code](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-requirements-errors-code) and [future_requirements.errors[].code](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-future_requirements-errors-code) enum properties on v1 objects, and to the [requirements.entries[].errors[].code](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_account_object-requirements-entries-errors-code) and [future_requirements.entries[].errors[].code](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_account_object-future_requirements-entries-errors-code) enum properties on v2 Accounts:

- `invalid_address_cmra_address`: Returned when an account’s address is identified as a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) or virtual mailbox address. To resolve this error, the account holder must update their address.
- `invalid_address_registered_agent_address`: Returned when an account’s address is identified as a registered agent address. To resolve this error, the account holder can update their address or upload a proof-of-address document.

For GA users, these new values provide more specific errors when we can’t accept an account address.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Integrations that read requirement error codes from Accounts v1 or Accounts v2 can now receive `invalid_address_cmra_address` and `invalid_address_registered_agent_address`. If your code uses strict enum matching or doesn’t handle unknown error codes, it can fail when it encounters these values.

## Impact

If your integration reads requirement errors from a v1 [Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), a v1 [Bank Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_bank_accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), a v1 [Capability](https://docs.stripe.com/api/capabilities/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), a v1 [Person](https://docs.stripe.com/api/persons/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), or a [v2 Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), update its error-handling logic to support `invalid_address_cmra_address` and `invalid_address_registered_agent_address`. Review [address validation for commercial compliance](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/commercial-compliance/address-validation.md) for integration guidance.

# Returns specific decline codes for BLIK payment failures

## What’s new

Replaces the [generic_decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#generic_decline) decline code with [code_invalid](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#code-invalid), [code_expired](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#code-expired), [insufficient_funds](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#partner_insufficient_funds), [customer_declined](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#customer-declined), [payment_limit_exceeded](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#payment_limit_exceeded), and [partner_generic_decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/codes.md#partner_generic_decline) for applicable BLIK payment failures.

Integrations with strict decline-code handling must accept `code_invalid`, `code_expired`, `insufficient_funds`, `customer_declined`, `payment_limit_exceeded`, and `partner_generic_decline`. Previously, API versions before Endive received `generic_decline`.

You now receive specific decline codes for applicable BLIK payment failures. Update your error handling to support `code_invalid`, `code_expired`, `insufficient_funds`, `customer_declined`, `payment_limit_exceeded`, and `partner_generic_decline`. # Sets canConfirm to false while updates are pending in Elements with Checkout Sessions

## What’s new

Updates [canConfirm](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/session_object#custom_checkout_session_object-canConfirm) to `false` while a Custom Checkout server update is queued or in progress. After all pending updates finish, `canConfirm` reflects whether the checkout is otherwise ready for confirmation. This provides a signal that integrations can use to avoid confirming with outdated information.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Elements with Checkout Sessions changes `canConfirm` to `false` while updates are pending, which could change behavior if you rely on `canConfirm` in your checkout flow. Previously, Stripe.js didn’t change `canConfirm` while server updates were pending.

## Impact

Your integration can prevent customers from confirming with outdated information by allowing confirmation only when `canConfirm` is `true`. Make sure that your integration handles the updated information when the pending requests resolve, and updates the state of your confirmation control when `canConfirm` changes. See [Submit the payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment.md?payment-ui=elements&api-integration=checkout#submit-payment) for implementation examples.

changes.statement: canConfirm is false while Checkout Session updates are pending

# Adds support for Data Share Only for 3D Secure authentication

## What’s new

Adds `data_share_only` as a possible 3D Secure (3DS) result in the [three_d_secure.result](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#charge_object-payment_method_details-card-three_d_secure-result) enum. This is included in the [payment_method_details](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#charge_object-payment_method_details) hash for [Charge](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [SetupAttempt](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_attempts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [PaymentRecord](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), and [PaymentAttemptRecord](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-attempt-record/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) resources.

This value indicates an issuer performed 3DS authentication using [Data Share Only](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/data-only.md) mode, a flow where cardholder data is shared with the issuer to allow them to make better authorization decisions.

Charge events (such as [charge.succeeded](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive&#event_types-charge.succeeded) and [charge.captured](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/types.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive&#event_types-charge.captured)) now include the `three_d_secure` object for Data Share Only transactions.

## Why is this a breaking change?

This change adds a new enum value to `three_d_secure.result`. This change affects behavior that depends on the existence of `three_d_secure` or the value of `three_d_secure.result`.

## Impact

Previously, Data Share Only 3DS authentications were indistinguishable from charges with no 3DS because the `three_d_secure` property was `null` in both cases. With this change, you can identify which transactions used [Data Share Only](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/data-only.md).

If your integration checks `three_d_secure.result` property, you can update it to handle the new `data_share_only` value. Only Data Share Only transactions after September 30, 2026 are exposed to this change.

# Rejects duplicate references for pending India card mandates

## What’s new

Rejects duplicate references associated with an India recurring card mandate that’s pending when creating a [Payment Intent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) or [Setup Intent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). Previously, validation only rejected references associated with an active mandate.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Requests that reuse a reference associated with a pending mandate now return a `resource_already_exists` error during intent creation or confirmation. Previously, these requests could succeed while the previous mandate was pending.

## Impact

Use a unique reference for each distinct India recurring card mandate. If you reuse a reference from a pending mandate, your request now returns `resource_already_exists`. See the [India recurring payments guide](https://docs.stripe.com/india-recurring-payments.md) for more information.

# Updates Financial Connections Session defaults

## What’s new

Standardizes [Financial Connections Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) defaults across account holder types.

- The [limits[accounts]](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-limits-accounts) parameter defaults to no maximum on the number of accounts an end user can link.
- The [manual_entry[mode]](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-manual_entry-mode) parameter defaults to `disabled`.
- The [filters[require_payment_method_support]](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-filters-require_payment_method_support) parameter defaults to `none`, so accounts aren’t required to support payments or to successfully retrieve account and routing numbers.
- The [filters[account_subcategories]](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-filters-account_subcategories) parameter defaults to all supported subcategories: `checking`, `savings`, `mortgage`, `line_of_credit`, and `credit_card`.
- The [filters[country]](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-filters-country) parameter defaults to the requesting merchant’s country when supported, and otherwise defaults to the US.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, some Sessions used account holder-specific defaults when optional configuration parameters were omitted. For example, Sessions created for connected accounts could default to collecting one checking or savings account, requiring payment method support, enabling automatic manual entry, and using the connected account’s country.

After upgrading, the same request can create a Session that allows more accounts and account types, no longer guarantees that linked accounts support payments, disables manual entry, or uses a different default country.

## Impact

If your integration relies on the previous implicit behavior, specify the configuration you require when creating the Session. For example, explicitly set `limits[accounts]`, `filters[account_subcategories]`, `filters[require_payment_method_support]`, `filters[country]`, and `manual_entry[mode]` instead of relying on their defaults.

Set `filters[require_payment_method_support]` to `all` or `at_least_one` if your integration requires payment-eligible accounts and successful account and routing number retrieval. If you set `manual_entry[mode]` to `automatic`, you must also configure payment method support. Automatic manual entry isn’t supported when `filters[require_payment_method_support]` is `none`.

## Upgrade

#### REST API

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.

3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

# Shows pending-authorization UI for MB WAY, Bizum, and BLIK with stripe.handleNextAction

## What’s new

Adds pending-authorization instructions to [stripe.handleNextAction](https://docs.stripe.com/js/payment_intents/handle_next_action) when a customer needs to approve an MB WAY payment in the MB WAY app or a Bizum or BLIK payment in their bank’s mobile app. Previously, `stripe.handleNextAction` waited for authorization without displaying this UI. This change makes its behavior consistent with `stripe.confirmPayment`.

## Why is this a breaking change?

If your integration displays its own MB WAY, Bizum, or BLIK authorization instructions while `stripe.handleNextAction` is pending, customers might see both your instructions and Stripe’s modal. Previous Stripe.js major versions retain the existing behavior. Remove or adjust any custom pending-authorization UI when upgrading to avoid showing duplicate instructions.

## Impact

Customers receive instructions to open the MB WAY app or their bank’s mobile app for Bizum and BLIK and approve the payment while Stripe.js waits for authorization. This prevents checkout from appearing unresponsive and reduces the need for integrations to implement payment-method-specific authorization messaging. When upgrading, remove or adjust custom pending-authorization UI to avoid duplicate instructions. See [Finalize payments on the server](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/finalize-payments-on-the-server.md#next-actions) for guidance on handling next actions with `stripe.handleNextAction`.

# Adds page limit validation for dispute evidence

## What’s new

Stripe now validates the estimated compiled page count of [evidence](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_dispute-evidence) submitted when you [update a Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). If the estimated page count of your text fields and file uploads exceeds the network page limit, the API returns a `400` [error](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) with the code `dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded`. This validation applies whether or not you set [submit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_dispute-submit) to `true`, so you can catch oversized evidence before final submission.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, you could [update a Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/api/disputes/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) with evidence of any length. Now, if the evidence exceeds the compiled page limit, the requset fails and returns a `400` `invalid_request_error` with the code `dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded`.

## Impact

If your integration submits [Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes.md) evidence through the API, requests that exceed the page limit now return a `400` error instead of succeeding. Update your error handling to check for the `dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded` error code. To resolve the error, shorten text fields or reduce the number of pages in uploaded files to stay within the limit.

## Changes

#### REST API

| Code | Change | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dispute_evidence_page_limit_exceeded` | Added | `Invoice.last_finalization_error`, `PaymentIntent.last_payment_error`, `SetupAttempt.setup_error`, `SetupIntent.last_setup_error`, `StripeError`, `Terminal.Reader.action.api_error` |

#### Node.js

| Code | Change | |
| --- | --- | --- |

# Makes Payment Evaluation signal scores nullable

## What’s new

Makes the [score](https://docs.stripe.com/api/radar/payment-evaluation/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#radar_payment_evaluation_object-signals-fraudulent_payment-score) property nullable for all [signals](https://docs.stripe.com/api/radar/payment-evaluation/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#radar_payment_evaluation_object-signals) in [Payment Evaluations](https://docs.stripe.com/api/radar/payment-evaluation/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). Radar Standard users receive `null` for `score`. Other eligible Radar plans continue to return rounded numeric scores.

Radar Standard users must now use API version `2026-09-30.endive` or later for all [Payment Evaluation](https://docs.stripe.com/api/radar/payment-evaluation.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) requests.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Integrations that expect `score` to always contain a number can fail when it returns `null`. Previously, an unavailable score returned `-1`. After upgrading, it returns `null` instead.

Radar Standard users receive a `payment_evaluation_on_api_version_not_supported` error (HTTP status 403) when making a Payment Evaluation request using an API version earlier than `2026-09-30.endive`. Previously, these requests succeeded.

## Impact

Before upgrading, update your integration to handle `null` signal scores and replace checks for `-1` with checks for `null`. When a score isn’t available, use the corresponding signal’s `risk_level` property, such as [fraudulent_payment.risk_level](https://docs.stripe.com/api/radar/payment-evaluation/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#radar_payment_evaluation_object-signals-fraudulent_payment-risk_level). Risk levels remain available to Radar Standard users.

If you use Radar Standard, [upgrade your API version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#how-can-i-upgrade-my-api) to `2026-09-30.endive` or later to continue using Payment Evaluations.

# Distinguishes platform-initiated account rejections from Stripe rejections

## What’s new

Updates the [requirements.disabled_reason](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-requirements-disabled_reason) and [future_requirements.disabled_reason](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-future_requirements-disabled_reason) properties on the [v1 Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) object to distinguish between platform-initiated rejections and Stripe rejections. Previously, platform-rejected accounts returned `rejected.fraud`, `rejected.terms_of_service`, or `rejected.other` for these properties. They now return:

- `rejected.platform_fraud` instead of `rejected.fraud`
- `rejected.platform_terms_of_service` instead of `rejected.terms_of_service`
- `rejected.platform_other` instead of `rejected.other`

## Why is this a breaking change?

The values returned in `requirements.disabled_reason` and `future_requirements.disabled_reason` for your platform-rejected accounts change when you upgrade to this API version. If your integration checks the previous values to identify platform rejections, you need to update this logic to handle the new values. You can now use these properties to determine whether the platform or Stripe rejected the account.

## Impact

Update any rejection-handling logic that checks `requirements.disabled_reason` or `future_requirements.disabled_reason` to handle the new `rejected.platform_*` values. See the versioned [Account API reference](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-requirements-disabled_reason) for all supported rejection reasons.

## Changes

| | Change | Event type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `account.updated` | Changed | `Event` |

#### Node.js

This change doesn’t affect the Node.js SDK.

# Unifies the billing cycle anchor format across Subscriptions and Invoices

## What’s new

Unifies how updates to a subscription’s billing cycle anchor are formatted when [updating Subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_subscription-billing_cycle_anchor), [resuming Subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/resume.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#resume_subscription-billing_cycle_anchor), and [creating Preview Invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/create_preview.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_invoice-subscription_details-billing_cycle_anchor). The [billing_cycle_anchor](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_subscription-billing_cycle_anchor) field now uses a consistent object format with a `type` field, replacing the previous string, enum, and timestamp formats.

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `billing_cycle_anchor` field now requires an object with a `type` field instead of a string value (for example, `{type: 'now'}`). When creating a preview invoice, the [subscription_details.billing_cycle_anchor](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/create_preview.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_invoice-subscription_details-billing_cycle_anchor) field requires an object with `type` and `timestamp` fields.

## Impact

Previously, you could pass a string value when updating a subscription’s billing cycle anchor. Instead, set `billing_cycle_anchor` to an object with an equivalent `type` parameter.

- Replace `now` with `{type: 'now'}`.
- Replace `unchanged` with `{type: 'unchanged'}`.

When creating a preview invoice for a new subscription whose billing cycle anchor is a future timestamp, replace `1234567890` with `{type: 'timestamp', timestamp: 1234567890}`.

# Adds rejected status for Accounts v2 capabilities

## What’s new

Adds a `rejected` value to the [status](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_core_account_object-merchant) property of account capabilities on [Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). This status appears alongside the existing values `active`, `pending`, `restricted`, and `unsupported`.

The [status_details](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_core_account_object-merchant) property now provides specific codes that describe the reason for rejection:

- `rejected_fraud`
- `rejected_incomplete_verification`
- `rejected_listed`
- `rejected_other`
- `rejected_platform_fraud`
- `rejected_platform_other`
- `rejected_platform_terms_of_service`
- `rejected_terms_of_service`

These codes can appear in the capability status for [merchant](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_core_account_object-merchant), [recipient](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_core_account_object-recipient), and [storer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_core_account_object-storer) configurations.

For rejected accounts, API versions before `2026-09-30.endive` return:

- `restricted` instead of `rejected` for `status`
- `restricted_other` instead of a specific `rejected_*` code in `status_details`

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, rejected accounts provided a `status` of `restricted` with a `status_details` code of `requirements_past_due`.

When an account rejected, we now return more specific error codes that describe the rejection reason. If your integration uses the `restricted` status to identify rejected accounts, you must update your code to handle the `rejected` status and the associated detail codes.

## Impact

If your integration reads capability `status` or `status_details` values from Accounts v2 [Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) objects, you can now understand and handle the specific reasons a capability configuration was rejected.

These events also now include the `rejected` status for rejected accounts:

- [v2.core.account[configuration.customer].capability_status_updated](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/event-types.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_accounts_event_types-v2.core.account%5Bconfiguration.customer%5D.capability_status_updated)

- [v2.core.account[configuration.customer].updated](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/event-types.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_accounts_event_types-v2.core.account%5Bconfiguration.customer%5D.updated)

## Upgrade

#### REST API

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.
- If you don’t use an SDK, update your [API requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api-versions.md#how-versions-are-specified-in-requests) to include `Stripe-Version: 2026-09-30.endive`
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

#### Node.js

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#view-your-api-version-and-the-latest-available-upgrade-in-workbench) in Workbench.
2. Upgrade your Node SDK to the latest version.
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).
6. In Workbench, [perform the upgrade](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#perform-the-upgrade). You can [roll back the version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#roll-back-your-api-version) for 72 hours.

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

## Related changes

- [Adds address validation errors for CMRAs and registered agents to Accounts v1 and Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/address-validation-cmra-registered-agents-accounts-v2.md)
- [Replaces the generic fraud rejection reason with specific fraud reasons](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/updated-reject-reason-codes.md)
- [Removes the configurations parameter from the Account Links v2 API](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/removes-configurations-parameter-from-v2-core-account-links-api.md)
- [Standardizes SEPA Direct Debit payment settings in the Accounts API](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/sepa-debit-settings-accounts.md)
- [Shows errors for eventually due requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/shows-errors-for-eventually-due-requirements.md)
- [Distinguishes platform-initiated account rejections from Stripe rejections](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/platform-rejection-reasons.md)
- [Adds additional shared fields to customer sharing](https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/additional-shared-fields-customer-sharing.md)

# Removes support for the payment method types option in Elements

## What’s new

Removes support for setting [paymentMethodTypes](https://docs.stripe.com/js/elements_object/create_without_intent#stripe_elements_no_intent-options-paymentMethodTypes) when you create Elements without a Payment or Setup Intent or call [elements.update()](https://docs.stripe.com/js/elements_object/update). Use `allowedPaymentMethodTypes` to limit available payment methods, or use [Dynamic Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) to manage them from the Dashboard.

## Why is this a breaking change?

If your integration sets `paymentMethodTypes`, Stripe.js now throws an integration error and prevents the Elements instance from being created or updated.

## Impact

You can no longer set `paymentMethodTypes` in your Elements options on Endive. Remove it, replace it with `allowedPaymentMethodTypes` to limit available payment methods, or manage payment methods in the Dashboard. Previously, Stripe.js versions through Dahlia supported `paymentMethodTypes`.

# Removes the payment method types parameter from Checkout Sessions

## What’s new

Removes the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) parameter from the [create Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) method. You can no longer pass `payment_method_types` when you create a Checkout Session. Use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) to manage payment methods from the Dashboard without writing code.

You can also use [excluded_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-excluded_payment_method_types) to exclude specific payment methods from the dynamic payment methods results or the new [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types) parameter to specify a set of payment methods.

The [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types) parameter accepts an array of payment method type and filters the list to only compatible payment methods based on other parameters such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. The compatible subset is shown in the [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#checkout_session_object-payment_method_types) property of the response.

Previously, [payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-08-26.dahlia#create_checkout_session-payment_method_types) returned an error when you specified an incompatible payment method. `allowed_payment_method_types` silently filters out incompatible methods and returns only those that work with the current configuration.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Passing `payment_method_types` as a parameter when you [create a Checkout Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) now returns a `400` error. If your integration sets this parameter, you must remove it and migrate to [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-allowed_payment_method_types).

## Impact

This migration requires careful attention if your integration passes `payment_method_types` when creating a Checkout Session. You must update your integration to use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) or switch to `allowed_payment_method_types` to get automatic compatibility filtering instead of errors. Requests that include `payment_method_types` on this now return a `400` error.

## Changes

#### REST API

| Parameters | Change | Resources or endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowed_payment_method_types` | Added | [Checkout.Session](/api/checkout/sessions/object?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#checkout_session_object), [Checkout.Session#create](/api/checkout/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session) |
| `payment_method_types` | Removed | [Checkout.Session#create](/api/checkout/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session) |

#### Node.js

| Parameters | Change | Resources or methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowed_payment_method_types` | Added | [Checkout.Session](/api/checkout/sessions/object?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#checkout_session_object), [Checkout.SessionCreateParams](/api/checkout/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session) |
| `payment_method_types` | Removed | [Checkout.SessionCreateParams](/api/checkout/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session) |

## Upgrade

#### REST API

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.
- If you don’t use an SDK, update your [API requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api-versions.md#how-versions-are-specified-in-requests) to include `Stripe-Version: 2026-09-30.endive`
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

#### Node.js

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#view-your-api-version-and-the-latest-available-upgrade-in-workbench) in Workbench.
2. Upgrade your Node SDK to the latest version.
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).
6. In Workbench, [perform the upgrade](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#perform-the-upgrade). You can [roll back the version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#roll-back-your-api-version) for 72 hours.

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

# Removes PayTo-specific fields from Payment Methods

## What’s new

Removes the [payto](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) field (containing [account_number](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [bsb_number](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), and [pay_id](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive)) when you [update PaymentMethods](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). Previously, the API accepted these [PayTo](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payto.md)-specific fields with a `200` status but never persisted the values. You can still update other fields such as [billing_details](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_method-billing_details) and [metadata](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_method-metadata) for PayTo Payment Methods.

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `payto` parameter isn’t accepted when you [update a Payment Method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). If your integration sends `payto` or any of its sub-fields (`account_number`, `bsb_number`, `pay_id`) when updating a PayTo Payment Method, the request returns an error instead of a `200` status. Update your code to remove these fields from your requests.

## Impact

If your integration passes `payto`, `payto[account_number]`, `payto[bsb_number]`, or `payto[pay_id]` to [update a Payment Method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), those requests now return an error. Remove these fields from your update calls. No previously stored data is affected because the API never persisted these values.

## Changes

#### REST API

| Parameter | Change | Resources or endpoints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payto` | Removed | [PaymentMethod#update](/api/payment_methods/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_method) |

#### Node.js

| Parameter | Change | Resources or methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payto` | Removed | [PaymentMethodUpdateParams](/api/payment_methods/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_method) |

## Upgrade

#### REST API

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.
2. If you use an SDK, upgrade to the corresponding SDK version for this API version.
- If you don’t use an SDK, update your [API requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api-versions.md#how-versions-are-specified-in-requests) to include `Stripe-Version: 2026-09-30.endive`
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).

Learn more about [Stripe API upgrades](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md).

#### Node.js

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#view-your-api-version-and-the-latest-available-upgrade-in-workbench) in Workbench.

# Removes the configurations parameter from the Account Links v2 API

## What’s new

Removes the [configurations](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/account-links/create.md?api-version=2026-08-26.dahlia#v2_create_account_links-use_case-account_onboarding-configurations) parameter from the [use_case.account_onboarding](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/account-links/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_account_link_object-use_case-account_onboarding) and [use_case.account_update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/account-links/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_account_link_object-use_case-account_update) hashes when you [create a v2 Account Link](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/account-links/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). Previously, `configurations` accepted an array of configuration names (such as customer, merchant, or recipient) to specify which configurations should be onboarded or updated. Stripe now automatically determines which configurations require onboarding, making this parameter unnecessary.

## Why is this a breaking change?

This change removes the `configurations` parameter from the `account_onboarding` and `account_update` use cases in the Account Links v2 API. If your existing integration includes `configurations` when creating a v2 Account Link, those requests fail on API version `2026-09-30.endive` or later. To avoid errors, remove the `configurations` parameter from your [create Account Link](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/account-links/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) requests before upgrading.

## Impact

If your integration passes `configurations` in any `use_case` when creating a v2 Account Link, you must remove that parameter before upgrading to the `2026-09-30.endive` API version. Requests that include `configurations` now return an error.

# Removes the payment method types parameter from Payment Intents and Setup Intents

## What’s new

Removes `payment_method_types` as a writable parameter from the [create](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), and [confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/confirm.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) methods on Payment Intents, and from the [create](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) and [update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) methods on Setup Intents. Passing `payment_method_types` on this API version returns a 400 error with the code `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported`.

Use [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) to automatically determine available payment methods based on other parameters such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. If you need more control:

- Use [excluded_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_payment_intent-excluded_payment_method_types) to exclude specific types from the set determined by dynamic payment methods.
- Use [allowed_payment_method_types](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_payment_intent-allowed_payment_method_types) to specify a list of types you want to accept. Stripe filters out incompatible types instead of returning an error.

`payment_method_types` remains as a read-only property on the [Payment Intent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#payment_intent_object-payment_method_types) and [Setup Intent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#setup_intent_object-payment_method_types) objects, reflecting the computed list of available payment methods.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, `payment_method_types` accepted a list of payment method types to explicitly set which methods are available on a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent. This parameter is no longer writable. Requests that pass `payment_method_types` on the affected endpoints return a `400` error.

To migrate, use [Dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) and remove `payment_method_types` and manage available methods from your [payment method settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/payment_methods). Stripe automatically filters for compatibility. Use `excluded_payment_method_types` to exclude specific types per request.

If you need more control, you can also use `allowed_payment_method_types` to pass a list of types you want to accept, similar to the old `payment_method_types` parameter. Incompatible types are silently filtered rather than returning an error.

## Impact

If your integration passes `payment_method_types` when creating, updating, or confirming a Payment Intent or Setup Intent, remove it before upgrading to API version `2026-08-26.preview`. Replace it with [dynamic payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/dynamic-payment-methods.md) (optionally combined with `excluded_payment_method_types`), or use `allowed_payment_method_types`. Dynamic payment methods automatically handle compatibility filtering, so you no longer need to maintain eligibility logic in your code.

## Changes

#### REST API

| `payment_method_types` | Removed | [PaymentIntent#confirm](/api/payment_intents/confirm?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#confirm_payment_intent), [PaymentIntent#create](/api/payment_intents/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_payment_intent), [PaymentIntent#update](/api/payment_intents/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_intent), [SetupIntent#create](/api/setup_intents/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_setup_intent), [SetupIntent#update](/api/setup_intents/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_setup_intent) |

#### Node.js

| --- | --- | --- |
| `payment_method_types` | Removed | [PaymentIntentConfirmParams](/api/payment_intents/confirm?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#confirm_payment_intent), [PaymentIntentCreateParams](/api/payment_intents/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_payment_intent), [PaymentIntentUpdateParams](/api/payment_intents/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_payment_intent), [SetupIntentCreateParams](/api/setup_intents/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_setup_intent), [SetupIntentUpdateParams](/api/setup_intents/update?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#update_setup_intent) |

# Renames the countries filter to country on Financial Connections Sessions

## What’s new

Renames the [filters.countries](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_financial_connections_session-filters) parameter to [filters.country](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_financial_connections_session-filters-country) and changes its type from an array of strings to a single string when you [create a Financial Connections Session](https://docs.stripe.com/api/financial_connections/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). Previously, `filters.countries` accepted an array but used only the first element. The parameter now accepts a single country code, making this behavior explicit.

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `filters.countries` parameter no longer exists. If your code passes an array of country codes to `filters.countries`, you must replace it with `filters.country` and provide a single country code string. Passing the old parameter name or an array value results in an error.

## Impact

If your integration passes `filters.countries` as an array when creating a [Financial Connections](https://docs.stripe.com/financial-connections.md) Session, update it to use `filters.country` with a single string value.

## Changes

#### REST API

| `country` | Added | [FinancialConnections.Session#create.filters](/api/financial_connections/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-filters) |
| `countries` | Removed | [FinancialConnections.Session#create.filters](/api/financial_connections/sessions/create?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_create_session-filters), [FinancialConnections.Session.filters](/api/financial_connections/sessions/object?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#financial_connections_session_object-filters) |

# Standardizes SEPA Direct Debit payment settings in the Accounts API

## What’s new

The [sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_account-settings-sepa_debit_payments-creditor_id) property on [Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-settings) now returns Stripe’s country-specific shared [SEPA Creditor Identifier](https://support.stripe.com/questions/sepa-creditor-identifier-\(creditor-id\)) when an account doesn’t have a custom one. Previously, this property was omitted for accounts using the shared identifier.

You can now set a custom SEPA Creditor Identifier to be used for SEPA Direct Debit payments when you [create a v1 Account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive). In [Accounts v2](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), you can set a custom SEPA Creditor Identifier when you [create](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) or [update](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/update.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) a v2 Account using the [configuration.merchant.sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#v2_create_accounts-configuration-merchant) parameter.

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id` property on the Account object was previously omitted for accounts using Stripe’s shared SEPA Creditor Identifier. It now returns the shared identifier value. If your code relies on an omitted value to infer that an account uses the shared identifier, you must update your integration to handle the new response.

## Impact

If your integration checks whether `sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id` is null or undefined to determine whether an account uses a shared SEPA Creditor Identifier, update that logic. This property now returns the shared identifier value.

# Adds destination property and new enum values to Reserve Plans, Holds and Releases

## What’s new

Adds a [destination](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-destination) property to all three Reserve objects. You can now identify which balance holds reserved funds and where those funds go when they’re released:

- [Reserve Plans](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-destination) and [Reserve Holds](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/hold/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_hold_object-destination) now include `destination` to indicate where reserved funds are sent. Possible values are `risk_reserved`, `settlement_reserved`, and `other`. Previously, the destination was implicitly `risk_reserved`.
- [Reserve Releases](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/release/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_release_object-destination) now include `destination` to indicate where released funds are sent. Possible values are `payments` and `other`. Previously, the destination was implicitly `payments`.

Reserve Plans can now represent funds that remain reserved until you disable the plan. These plans have a [type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-type) of `manual_release`. When this value is present, the response includes a [manual_release](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-manual_release) property indicating that funds are released when the plan is disabled instead of on a schedule. In addition:

- The [type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-type) property adds `manual_release` and `other` to its existing `fixed_release` and `rolling_release` values.
- The [status](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-status) property adds `other` to its existing `active`, `disabled`, and `expired` values.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, every Reserve Plan and Reserve Hold used the `risk_reserved` balance, and every Reserve Release sent funds to the `payments` balance. Those assumptions are no longer valid.

If your integration uses them for reporting, reconciliation, or other reserve-specific logic, it might classify funds incorrectly unless it reads `destination` from each object.

Update your integration to check [Reserve Plan](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-destination), [Reserve Hold](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/hold/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_hold_object-destination), and [Reserve Release](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/release/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_release_object-destination) for destination-specific logic.

Reserve Plans can also return new [type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-type) and [status](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-status) values. Update your integration if it rejects unrecognized enum values.

## Impact

You can now represent risk and settlement reserves accurately, track where released funds are sent, and recognize plans that release funds only when disabled.

Before upgrading:

- Check the `destination` property on [Reserve Plan](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-destination), [Reserve Hold](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/hold/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_hold_object-destination), and [Reserve Release](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/release/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_release_object-destination) objects rather than assuming a destination.
- Support `manual_release` plans and use [manual_release](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-manual_release) to identify their release behavior.
- Handle the new Reserve Plan [type](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-type) and [status](https://docs.stripe.com/api/reserve/plan/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reserve_plan_object-status) values.

# Shows errors for eventually due requirements

## What’s new

In the [Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), [Persons](https://docs.stripe.com/api/persons.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive), and [Capabilities](https://docs.stripe.com/api/capabilities.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) APIs, validation and verification errors can now appear in the [requirements.errors](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-requirements-errors) and [future_requirements.errors](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-future_requirements-errors) arrays for [eventually_due](https://docs.stripe.com/api/accounts/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#account_object-future_requirements-eventually_due) requirements.

# Allows empty optional address fields in Elements with Checkout Sessions

## What’s new

Stops applying format validation to empty optional address fields in [Elements with the Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md). Previously, an empty optional field, such as a postal code in a country where postal codes aren’t required, could prevent confirmation because the empty value failed format validation.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Starting with Endive, customers can confirm a Checkout Session without entering address fields that are optional for their country. Previous Stripe.js major versions retain the stricter behavior, which might affect integrations that rely on Stripe.js to require these fields.

## Impact

Customers are no longer blocked from confirming because they left an optional address field empty. Stripe.js continues to validate the format when a customer provides a value. If your integration requires a field that Stripe considers optional, [collect and validate the address in your own form](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/collect-addresses.md?payment-ui=embedded-components) before confirming the Checkout Session.

# Requires billing details when Payment Element collection is disabled

## What’s new

Requires [Elements with the Checkout Sessions API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/quickstart.md) integrations to provide required billing details for any field disabled on the Payment Element, starting with Endive. If you set a billing field to `never` in the [Payment Element configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/create_payment_element#custom_checkout_create_payment_element-options-fields-billingDetails), the Payment Element no longer collects that field, and you’re responsible for supplying required billing data through another Element or a supported Custom Checkout SDK method.

If a required billing field is still missing when you call [checkout.confirm()](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/confirm), Stripe.js throws an integration error. Optional fields such as `address.line2` are exempt from this validation.

## Why is this a breaking change?

Previously, `checkout.confirm()` could succeed even when a required billing field configured as `never` wasn’t provided through another source. Starting with Endive, these integrations fail at confirmation with an integration error.

If you currently set any [fields.billingDetails](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/create_payment_element#custom_checkout_create_payment_element-options-fields-billingDetails) value to `never` without providing the corresponding required data, your integration is affected. Previous Stripe.js major versions retain the earlier behavior.

## Impact

If your integration disables any billing-details fields on the Payment Element, provide the corresponding data before calling `checkout.confirm()`. Use one of the following approaches depending on the type of billing data. For a full walkthrough of address collection with Custom Checkout, see [Collect physical addresses](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/collect-addresses.md).

If your integration collects specific billing details itself, set only those fields to `never` and leave the remaining fields as `auto`. The Payment Element can then collect the remaining fields when the selected payment method requires them.

Set `fields.billingDetails` to `never` only if your integration collects all billing details itself. In this configuration, the Payment Element doesn’t collect any billing details, so you must collect and provide every applicable billing field through another Element or supported Custom Checkout SDK method.

### Name and address

- Call [updateBillingAddress](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/update_billing_address) to set the billing address before confirmation.
- Pass a [billingAddress](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/confirm#custom_checkout_session_confirm-options-billingAddress) option to `checkout.confirm()`.
- Use the [Billing Address Element](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/create_billing_address_element) to collect billing addresses through a dedicated Element.

If you use automatic tax and disable billing address collection in the Payment Element, don’t pass `billingAddress` to `checkout.confirm()`. Instead, provide the tax address using the [Address Element](https://docs.stripe.com/elements/address-element.md) or `updateBillingAddress()`. See [Collect tax with Elements](https://docs.stripe.com/tax/checkout/elements.md) for details.

### Email

- Call [updateEmail](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/update_email) to set the email before confirmation.
- Pass an [email](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/confirm#custom_checkout_session_confirm-options-email) option to `checkout.confirm()`.

### Phone

- Enable [phone_number_collection.enabled](https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#create_checkout_session-phone_number_collection-enabled) on the Checkout Session.
- Call [updatePhoneNumber](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/update_phone_number) to set the phone number before confirmation.
- Pass a [phoneNumber](https://docs.stripe.com/js/custom_checkout/confirm#custom_checkout_session_confirm-options-phoneNumber) option to `checkout.confirm()`.

# Surfaces India card mandates on Charges and SetupIntents even when inactive

## What’s new

Changes the following properties for India recurring card payments so that they return the mandate ID even when registration fails and the mandate is `inactive`:

- [payment_method_details.card.mandate](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#charge_object-payment_method_details-card-mandate) property on [Charges](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive)
- [mandate](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#setup_intent_object-mandate) property on [SetupIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive)

Previously, these properties were `null` after a registration failure.

A mandate created for a [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) can also become `inactive` immediately, without first having a `pending` status.

## Why is this a breaking change?

If your integration treats a non-null `payment_method_details.card.mandate` property on a Charge or `mandate` property on a SetupIntent as confirmation that the mandate is usable, you must update it to check the mandate’s status. Attempting a subsequent off-session payment with an `inactive` mandate causes the payment to fail.

If your integration assumes that a newly created mandate always starts as `pending`, update it to handle an initial status of `inactive`. Don’t rely solely on `mandate.updated` events to determine whether the mandate becomes active.

## Impact

Before using a returned mandate for a subsequent off-session payment, retrieve it and verify that its status is `active`. You can also use an inactive mandate’s ID to identify a failed registration and show the failure to your customer. See [Mandate webhooks](https://docs.stripe.com/india-recurring-payments.md?integration=subscriptions#mandate-status-and-troubleshooting) for integration guidance.

## Upgrade

#### REST API

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/workbench/guides.md#view-api-versions) in Workbench.

3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).

5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).

#### Node.js

1. [View your current API version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#view-your-api-version-and-the-latest-available-upgrade-in-workbench) in Workbench.
2. Upgrade your Node SDK to the latest version.
3. Upgrade the API version used for [webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks/versioning.md).
4. [Test your integration](https://docs.stripe.com/testing.md) against the new version.
5. If you use Connect, [test your Connect integration](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/testing.md).
6. In Workbench, [perform the upgrade](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#perform-the-upgrade). You can [roll back the version](https://docs.stripe.com/upgrades.md#roll-back-your-api-version) for 72 hours.

# Replaces the generic fraud rejection reason with specific fraud reasons

## What’s new

Replaces the generic `fraud` value for the [reason](https://docs.stripe.com/api/account/reject.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive#reject_account-reason) parameter when [rejecting an account](https://docs.stripe.com/api/account/reject.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) with more specific fraud reasons:

- `fraud_payment_method_casher`
- `fraud_payment_method_tester`
- `fraud_no_intent_to_fulfill`
- `fraud_other`

The parameter now also supports `credit` as a new value. The existing values `terms_of_service` and `other` remain supported.

Also updates the `reason` parameter from a string to an enum in affected SDKs.

## Why is this a breaking change?

The `reason` parameter changes from a string to an enum that doesn’t include `fraud` as a value. Requests that pass `fraud` return an HTTP `400` error.

## Impact

If your integration [rejects connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/account/reject.md?api-version=2026-09-30.endive) for suspected fraud, update it to use one of the new fraud reasons that best describes the suspected activity. Use `fraud_other` when none of the more specific reasons apply.

Update your integration to use the new `reason` enum, including calls that continue to use `terms_of_service` or `other`.
